case.case_title: Joseph Perera Alias Bruten Perera v. The Attorney-General and Others

clause.text: No person shall be arrested except according to law and must be informed of the reason.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the arrest and detention of the petitioners were lawful and whether they were informed of the reasons for their arrest and detention in accordance with Article 13(1).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioners claimed that their fundamental rights under Article 13(1) were violated because they were arrested and detained unlawfully and were not informed of the reasons for their arrest and detention.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents argued that the arrest and detention were lawful under the Emergency Regulations, specifically Regulations 18 and 19, and that the petitioners were informed of the reasons for their arrest.
key_facts: Petitioners were arrested on 26 June 1986 before a public meeting at Luxmi Hall, Chilaw.
Police acted on complaints from the Principal of St. Mary’s College and Vice Principal of Ananda College about a meeting intended to create unrest among students.
Petitioners were found in possession of leaflets and documents alleged to bring the government into hatred and contempt.
Detention order was issued on 27 June 1986 under Emergency Regulations.
Petitioners were detained until 7 August 1986, with remand orders extending detention.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court held that under Article 13(1), no person shall be arrested except according to law and must be informed of the reason. The arrest is lawful if based on reasonable suspicion and the officer making the arrest must have reasonable grounds for suspecting the person to be involved in an offence. Informing the arrested person of the reason is required except in exceptional cases where it is obvious the person knows the reason.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The arresting officer, Sergeant Major Abeysinghe, had reasonable grounds based on complaints and possession of documents to suspect the petitioners of offences under the Emergency Regulations. He informed the petitioners of the reason for their arrest, satisfying the requirement of Article 13(1). The arrest was therefore lawful. However, the detention beyond the reasonable period for investigation was unlawful.
principles_established: Arrest must be based on reasonable suspicion with objective grounds.
The arrested person must be informed of the reason for arrest unless it is obvious.
Detention must be for a reasonable period necessary for investigation.
precedents_cited: Eshugbayi Eleko v. Govt. of Nigeria (1931) AC 662
Hussien v. Chog Fook Kam (1969) 3 ALL ER 1626
Nanayakkara v. Henry Perera and Others (1985) 2 Sri LR 375

outcome.holding: The court held that the initial arrest of the petitioners was lawful and in accordance with Article 13(1) as they were informed of the reasons. However, the detention beyond 15 July 1986 was unlawful as the investigation was complete by then and no further lawful basis existed for detention.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The petitioners were awarded compensation of Rs. 10,000 each for unlawful detention and Rs. 3,000 each as costs.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(1) is central to the court's reasoning on the legality of the arrest and detention, focusing on whether the petitioners were lawfully arrested and informed of the reasons, and whether their detention was lawful.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: Sergeant Major Abeysinghe stated he informed the petitioners of the reason for their arrest for distributing documents bringing the government into hatred and contempt. The court found the arrest lawful but detention beyond 15 July 1986 unlawful.
